0.headline: Paras Healthcare IPO booked 39% so far on Day 3: retail portion subscribed 1.5x
0.heading: Paras Healthcare IPO booked 39% so far on Day 3: retail portion subscribed 1.5x
0.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) for Paras Healthcare continued its subdued demand on the third day of bidding, with the issue receiving 39 percent subscription by 10:55 am on October 23, as per NSE data.
0.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) for Paras Healthcare continued its subdued demand on the third day of bidding, with the issue receiving 39 percent subscription by 10:55 am on October 23, as per NSE data.

The Rs 1,450-crore IPO received bids for 47,29,725 shares against 1,20,83,331 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand, subscribing to 1.5 times of their allotted portion, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 31 percent.

In the grey market, the Paras Healthcare IPO was commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 9 per share on the morning of October 23, as per Investorgain. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 693, the premium indicated a potential listing gain of around 1.3 percent.

Read Also: Tonbo Imaging shares list at 66% premium on BSE, NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?

The grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and is based on transactions outside the regulated stock exchanges. It is not a guarantee of listing performance, and the premium can fluctuate before the shares make their stock market debut.

The Paras Healthcare IPO will remain open for public subscription from October 21 to October 23. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 660–693 per share.

The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 950 crore, taking the total issue size to Rs 1,450 crore.

Under the OFS, promoter Dharminder Kumar Nagar will sell shares worth Rs 300 crore, while Commelina, an affiliate of private equity firm Creador, will offload shares worth Rs 650 crore.

Ahead of the IPO, Paras Healthcare raised Rs 652.5 crore through its anchor book. The company allotted 94.15 lakh equity shares to 21 institutional investors on Monday.

Global investors participating in the anchor book included the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock Global Funds, Eastspring Investments, Government Pension Fund Global, Natixis International Funds, Integrated Core Strategies (Asia) and Citigroup Global.

Paras Healthcare plans to utilise Rs 375 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue to repay a portion of its outstanding debt. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

The IPO proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, while the OFS component will be received by the selling shareholders.

Paras Healthcare provides tertiary and quaternary healthcare services through a network of eight hospitals operating under the Paras brand. The hospitals have a combined capacity of 2,211 beds across North India, Bihar and Jharkhand.

As part of its expansion strategy, the company plans to add a 300-bed hospital in Gurugram and a 500-bed facility in Ludhiana. The two hospitals are expected to become operational in the current and next financial years, respectively.

The expansion is aimed at increasing the company's hospital capacity and strengthening its presence in key healthcare markets.

JM Financial, BofA Securities India and Nuvama Wealth Management are the merchant bankers to the Paras Healthcare IPO.

1.headline: Wiscon Industries IPO to open on October 27 with price band at Rs 194-204 per share
1.heading: Wiscon Industries IPO to open on October 27 with price band at Rs 194-204 per share
1.intro: Wiscon Industries IPO | The 53.92 lakh shares IPO comprises fresh issue of 43.14 lakh equity shares, and an offer-for-sale of 10.78 lakh shares.
1.body:
Consumer electronic products supplier Wiscon Industries tapped capital markets to raise funds up to Rs 110 crore via initial public offering for its capital expenditure and working capital requirements.

The company is set open its IPO for public subscription on October 27, with price band at Rs 194-204 per share, while the bidding will close on October 29.

The one-day anchor book for institutional investors will open on October 26, while its shares will be available for trading on the BSE SME platform on November 3.

The 53.92 lakh shares IPO comprises fresh issue of 43.14 lakh equity shares, and an offer-for-sale of 10.78 lakh shares.

Promoter Sidhant Dalmia will be selling shareholder in the offer-for-sale.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

New Delhi-based Wiscon Industries supplies several consumer electronic products including LED TVs, air coolers, washing machines and air conditioners under its flagship brand Wiscon, serving business-to-business as well as business-to-customers within India.

Business-to-business segment contributed nearly 99 percent to revenue in the fiscal 2026, and the remaining contribution came from the business-to-customers segment.

The company will invest Rs 50 crore of net fresh issue proceeds in its subsidiary Dalmia Technologies for financing its capital expenditure towards purchase of plant and machinery, and incremental working capital requirements. Further, the 17 crore will be used for company's working capital requirements, Rs 5.2 crore for marketing and promotional activities, and the remainder funds for general corporate purposes.

The merchant banker managing the Wiscon Industries IPO is Smart Horizon Capital Advisors.

2.headline: Sahajanand Medical Technologies shares debut at 8% premium on NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?
2.heading: Sahajanand Medical Technologies shares debut at 8% premium on NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?
2.intro: Shares of Sahajanand Medical Technologies made a positive debut on the stock exchanges on October 23, listing at a premium of nearly 8% over the company's initial public offering (IPO) price.
2.body:
Shares of Sahajanand Medical Technologies made a positive debut on the stock exchanges on October 23, listing at a premium of nearly 8 percent over the company's initial public offering (IPO) price.

The shares listed at Rs 371.15 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), marking a premium of 7.89 percent over the issue price of Rs 344 per share. On the BSE, the stock debuted at Rs 368.05, up 6.99 percent from the IPO price.

Following the listing, Sahajanand Medical Technologies' market capitalisation stood at around Rs 3,741.11 crore.

The listing was stronger than grey market expectations. The shares were commanding a grey market premium (GMP), indicating an estimated listing gain of around 5 percent on the morning of October 23, according to Investorgain.

Read Also: Tonbo Imaging shares list at 66% premium on BSE, NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?

The Rs 475.48-crore IPO was subscribed 14.20 times by the close of bidding on October 19, according to NSE data. The issue received bids for 13,84,72,771 shares against 97,50,482 shares on offer.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, subscribing to their allotted portion 34.70 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 14.64 times, while the retail investor portion was subscribed 3.03 times.

The IPO was open for subscription from October 15 to October 19. The company raised Rs 475.48 crore through an offer for sale (OFS) of approximately 1.38 crore equity shares.

Check IPO News Here

Since the issue was entirely an OFS, the proceeds will go to the selling shareholders, and the company will not receive any funds from the IPO.

Should you buy, sell or hold?

Sarvam Goel, Founder of Pocketful, said, "Investors who received allotment should hold, and those who missed the IPO can look to add post-listing."

About Sahajanand Medical Technologies

Mumbai-headquartered Sahajanand Medical Technologies develops medical devices used in cardiovascular and vascular interventions. Its product portfolio includes coronary stents and coronary balloons, along with structural heart products such as transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) devices and occluders.

The company also offers renal stents under its own brand and peripheral drug-coated balloons (DCBs). Its products are used in medical procedures to treat cardiovascular conditions and other vascular disorders.
